contexts.context: Repository Scanning & Scoring/CI Gate & Status Checks
contexts.name: CI Gate & Status Checks

subjects.subject: quality-gates
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/org-gate.ts:23 A stored gate policy that cannot be parsed turns into null, so both the public gate route and the App check run use the weaker archetype default instead of refusing to give a verdict; the route's own 503 fail-closed path (it assumes null only ever means unset) never fires, and org-gate.test.ts:78 locks this behaviour in.

subjects.subject: hitl-approval
subjects.evidence: src/app/api/org/gate-policy/route.ts:251 The owner's change to the merge-blocking bar is committed by setOrgGatePolicy first, and the audit record is written afterwards in a separate step whose failure is swallowed, so the bar can be loosened with no record of it, which is the 'opening with no witness' defect decision-records forbids.

subjects.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
subjects.evidence: src/lib/scoring/gate.ts:1 The gate folds policy over a finished maturity report and posts check runs. It calls no model and holds no tool loop, hook chain, code loading or conversation state. Searches of src/lib/scoring, src/app/api/gate, src/lib/github, src/app/api/org/gate-policy and src/lib/db for runToolLoop, maxLegs, plugin and checkpointMode found nothing. Its 'llm' hits are only scan cache-key suffixes.

subjects.subject: admission-queue
subjects.evidence: src/app/api/org/gate-policy/route.ts:56 The sweep deadline is independently hard-coded rather than computed from the route's execution ceiling, allowing the protective bound and destructive timeout to drift.

subjects.subject: conformance-checking
subjects.evidence: src/lib/scoring/gate.ts:552 The gate's outcome vocabulary is only failures plus skipped. It has no 'known, accepted, dated' class and no repo-level exemption with an expiry, so a failure someone has accepted is reported red on every run until an org admin lowers the bar for the whole org.

subjects.subject: prompt-assembly
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/openai.ts:92 Every provider sends the one assembled assessment and Bedrock puts one cache cut on the stable system block, but the response reservation is an env default (4096, config.ts:135) that measured output length never feeds back into, and a cut response throws telling the operator to raise the env rather than retrying once at a higher ceiling.

subjects.subject: eval-harness
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/matrix-scores.ts:59 The model scorecard publishes a best-first order (and bestModel() recommends rank[0] as the org pin) from a single-trial, n=10 matrix that records no within-condition SD, so no spread-versus-noise check can precede the ranking.

subjects.subject: voice-io
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/provider.ts:94 The provider interface has one method, a text assessment that returns maturity scores. It has no transcription or synthesis direction, and a search of src/lib/llm and src/ found no speech APIs, so voice-io's engine layer does not exist here.

subjects.subject: agent-cli-transport
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/transport/claude.ts:109 The authorization probe inherits credentials that real runs strip, so it can report authorization for a different billing environment.

subjects.subject: test-harness
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/bedrock.test.ts:18 Provider suites swap the vendor SDK class for hand-built response shapes, so the seam sits above the client library's serialization layer and nothing would notice an upstream change. The only real-provider lane (llm-bench, LLM_BENCH=1) is opt-in, manual and kept out of CI.

subjects.subject: codebase-scanning
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/provider.ts:311 validateAssessment drops a malformed model claim (unknown facet, a dimension that is not scored, missing path or quote) with a bare `continue` and never counts it. The same happens to roadmap entries and discrepancies, so a reply where most claims cite rules that don't exist looks like a quiet, smaller reply instead of a degraded one, which llm-assisted-scanning names as its failure.

subjects.subject: settings
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/config.ts:43 Malformed numeric LLM configuration silently becomes the default without the corruption diagnostic required by typed accessors.

subjects.subject: multi-provider-gateway-plane
subjects.evidence: src/lib/scan-assess.ts:353 The multi-provider attempt loop continues after any non-client exception without router-versus-candidate attribution, allowing an application-side defect to consume subsequent candidates.

subjects.subject: structured-output
subjects.evidence: src/lib/llm/provider.ts:236 The validator silently rounds and clamps model scores into legal values instead of rejecting invalid values or producing an explicit repair outcome.

contexts.context: Repository Scanning & Scoring/Maturity Model & Scoring Engine
contexts.name: Maturity Model & Scoring Engine

subjects.subject: prompt-assembly
subjects.evidence: src/lib/scoring/prompt.ts:91 buildAssessmentPrompt is one pure assembler with a stable system prefix, but the standing text opens on an expertise claim and the file window is spent by character-slicing evidence the model cannot fetch back.

subjects.subject: translation-quality-measurement
subjects.evidence: src/lib/maturity/model.ts:1 This module is a rubric for scoring engineering maturity, not a store of machine-translated text. A case-insensitive search of src/lib, src/components and src/app found no hits for pretranslat, termbase, i18next, next-intl or machine translation, and package.json has no i18n dependency, so there is no derived translation store for the subject to measure.

subjects.subject: eval-harness
subjects.evidence: scripts/benchmark.mjs:110 The calibration harness can exit successfully under --strict after every case errors or after only a passing subset returns, so incomplete evaluation can satisfy the gate.

subjects.subject: agent-instruction-files
subjects.evidence: src/lib/analyze/guidance-quality.ts:24 The D1 guidance grader awards 6 points whenever a guidance file has an architecture, overview, directory-structure or layout section. That pays repos for the reachable "describe your repo" overview that the standard measures as buying nothing at higher cost per session, even though r18 already stopped paying for length on exactly that cost argument.

subjects.subject: docs-sync
subjects.evidence: src/lib/analyze/platform-signals.ts:126 The analyzer's documented scoring award maps only to scan.md, leaving the maturity-model reference's explicit description of that award outside the change obligation.

subjects.subject: docs-sync
subjects.evidence: src/lib/scan.ts:29 The pipeline delegates behavior to four phase modules that match no source-doc mapping entry, leaving changes in those modules invisible to the documentation obligation.

subjects.subject: codebase-scanning
subjects.evidence: src/lib/scan-ingest.ts:148 The scan pipeline isolates per-sensor failures, carries skips in the snapshot, excludes unobservable absence checks, budgets ingestion and LLM calls, and guards persistence against unauthoritative or truncated runs.

subjects.subject: supply-chain
subjects.evidence: src/lib/security/checks.ts:218 A committed Dependabot or Renovate file scores 10 with no check that any update proposal was opened, so a configured-but-dead lane reads as covered.

subjects.subject: eval-harness
subjects.evidence: src/app/api/scan/route.ts:8 These files are the product's scan protocol adapters (JSON and SSE), the scan form, and their deterministic route tests; they run no candidate models against declared scenarios. A search of the context's files found no judge, trial, holdout, golden-set or anchor-set constructs, and only product 'rubric' and 'baseline' wording.

subjects.subject: deterministic-prefix-caching
subjects.evidence: src/app/api/scan/route.ts:183 The only cache in this context stores the whole finished ScanReport for one commit (owner/repo@sha::mode), served on a re-request. There is no per-sample transform chain re-applied over training epochs, no deterministic head followed by a random augmentation tail, and no seam to find, so the subject's precondition does not hold. Searching src/app and src/components for randomizable, augmentation, dataloader and num_workers found nothing; the only 'cacheable prefix' hits are about LLM prompt caching, in src/lib/scoring and src/lib/llm, outside this context.

subjects.subject: settings
subjects.evidence: src/lib/github/host.ts:17 The shared endpoint accessor normalizes arbitrary nonblank strings without URL validation, allowing malformed deployment configuration to reach consumers as a usable host value.

subjects.subject: docs-sync
subjects.evidence: scripts/docs/feature-doc-map.json:82 One wide glob couples every file here to github-app.md, whose key-files table names only governance.ts of this context. The prose that actually describes these modules (scan.md for source.ts, auth.md for discover.ts, org-intelligence.md for codeowners.ts, forges.md for host.ts) is coupled to none of them, so the map reports membership while pointing at the wrong document.

subjects.subject: data-access
subjects.evidence: src/lib/github/governance.ts:71 A successful branch response containing an object without a valid protected boolean becomes a confident protection verdict instead of a distinguishable decoding failure.

subjects.subject: multi-provider-gateway-plane
subjects.evidence: src/lib/github/list.ts:116 Context searches found no finish_reason, tool_calls, or failover constructs, and the inspected fallback changes GitHub resource paths on one configured API rather than selecting interchangeable upstream implementations.

subjects.subject: terminal-multiplexing
subjects.evidence: src/lib/auth.ts:326 This context maintains authentication cookies rather than interactive terminal sessions, and searches of its files, surrounding auth directories, and repository found no xterm, multiplexer, scrollback, or node-pty references.

subjects.subject: concurrent-vcs
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/sessions.ts:2 "Session" here means a signed login cookie with a revocation version, not a working session in a shared checkout. The OAuth and session code performs no VCS operations. A ripgrep of src/app/api/auth, src/app/auth, src/lib/supabase, src/lib/db and src/lib found no read-tree, git stash or update-index.

subjects.subject: session-continuation
subjects.evidence: src/app/auth/callback/route.ts:83 Context and repository searches found no loopAuthority, pendingStop or candidateYield identifiers, and inspection shows browser authentication rather than the agent continuation loop this subject governs.

subjects.subject: agent-instruction-files
subjects.evidence: src/lib/standard/maintain.ts:183 The guidance projection generator hardcodes an inlined per-host regex branch rather than compiling from a declarative host contract, preventing extensible transformation of tool vocabularies or frontmatter across different agent hosts.

subjects.subject: conformance-checking
subjects.evidence: src/lib/standard/types.ts:32 The standard's capability verification write-back persists a naked boolean without timestamp, standard version, rung provenance, or proof lifetime expiry.

subjects.subject: standards-layered-runtime
subjects.evidence: src/lib/standard/index.ts:65 Context and repository searches found no registrar or WinterCG matches, and this entry point generates repository artifacts rather than assembling an embeddable language runtime.

subjects.subject: repo-manifest-standard
subjects.evidence: src/lib/standard/manifest.ts:258 Regeneration reconstructs capability entries using only owned fields, discarding foreign metadata and violating the writer-side preservation rule.

subjects.subject: untrusted-extension-host
subjects.evidence: src/lib/standard/index.ts:1 This module generates files (manifest, doctor.mjs, guardrails, memory) that Ascent writes into a customer repo, so Ascent is the author of that code, not a host running untrusted code. The 'extension' hits are YAML extension fields, and the new Function calls appear only in standard.test.ts, where they evaluate Ascent's own generated parser source. A search of src/ for isolated-vm, quickjs, vm2, node:vm and extensionHost found no hits.

subjects.subject: voice-io
subjects.evidence: src/components/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx:6 The first-run wizard is a gate, pick, select and scan flow for repositories, with no voice setup step. The tour's 'narrated' and 'speaks' wording means displayed text. A search of src/components/onboarding, src/app/onboarding and src/ found no speech APIs, so voice-setup-experience's precondition (first-run voice onboarding) does not hold.

subjects.subject: mcp-tools
subjects.evidence: src/components/onboarding/importScan.ts:114 A case-insensitive search of src/app/onboarding and src/components/onboarding for mcp, inputSchema, tools/call and jsonrpc found nothing. The wizard is a browser UI posting to an ordinary app API, with no tool catalog, protocol dispatch or tool results.

subjects.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
subjects.evidence: src/app/onboarding/page.tsx:26 The wizard is a first-run door: GitHub sign-in, App install and an import scan. It never builds the code around a model call. Searches of src/components/onboarding and src/app/onboarding for runToolLoop, maxLegs, plugin and checkpointMode found nothing, and the only 'hook' hits are React hooks.

subjects.subject: wizard-flows
subjects.evidence: Refresh re-attach now works (src/components/onboarding/useOnboardingFlow.ts:194), but src/components/onboarding/useOnboardingFlow.ts:241 keeps the run pointer (runId) only in tab-scoped sessionStorage while the import outlives the tab (src/components/onboarding/useImportReattach.ts:6): a closed tab or second device reopens /onboarding on pick with no trace of the running run (src/app/api/org/import/route.ts:382 claim guard stops a double charge, not the lost pointer); and src/components/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.run.ts:182 decodes an unreadable snapshot as no snapshot, the silent fresh start snapshot-and-resume forbids.

subjects.subject: hitl-approval
subjects.evidence: src/components/onboarding/importScan.ts:111 The wizard's own import helper still enrols repos in the recurring billable weekly watch by default on the App path whenever a caller leaves out `watch`, and the server defaults it to true as well, so the spend consent lives only in a client module store and in each caller remembering to pass the field; this default has already re-subscribed declined repos once.

subjects.subject: admission-queue
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/scan-jobs.ts:196 Distinct jobs are persisted without checking aggregate backlog capacity, so request batch caps do not bound the durable queue.

subjects.subject: concurrent-vcs
subjects.evidence: src/app/api/org/import/route.ts:33 The "claim" in this context is a database ScanJob row that dedups concurrent scans of one repo, not a session's claim on paths in a shared git checkout. The routes scan via the GitHub API and persist to the DB; they never stage, commit, stash or create worktrees. A ripgrep of the import/repos/scan/watch/schedule/active/cron-rescan route dirs and src/lib/db found no read-tree, git stash or GIT_INDEX_FILE.

subjects.subject: runner-fleet
subjects.evidence: src/app/api/cron/rescan/route.ts:3 These routes run scan work as an application-level durable ScanJob queue, drained inside a Vercel serverless invocation with a fixed SCAN_CONCURRENCY. They do not provision, type, scale or isolate CI runners. The golden path hands application concurrency and job coordination to concurrency-guards and job-coordination. A search of the context's directories for runs-on, actions-runner, autoscal and hashFiles found nothing. The words 'queue', 'fleet' and 'runner' do appear, but they name the scan queue, the repo fleet and the standing-runner drive rows.

subjects.subject: codebase-scanning
subjects.evidence: src/app/api/org/import/route.ts:456,463 explicitly records recordScanOutcome(org, repo, { ok: false, error: msg }) on a per-repo scan failure inside the bulk import/rescan loop rather than swallowing it via .catch(()=>null) — realizes sensor-pipeline's 'every sensor failure isolated and reported as skipped, never silently empty' for the org-level sweep, in contrast to the sibling 'Scan Pipeline & Ingestion' context's recorded deviation (governance/posture/exposure fetches that DO swallow with score-bearing folds).

subjects.subject: audit-logging

subjects.subject: browser-credential-boundary
subjects.evidence: src/lib/register/data.ts:117-144 REGISTER_REPO_SELECT is a structural Prisma select carrying no sensitive/internal columns, and isPrivate is re-asserted at the scan query, the repo query, AND per-row in registerEntryFrom:155 — three independent checks, matching omit-the-column-not-the-value's structural-exclusion discipline; leaderboard/page.tsx:61 and portfolio.ts:80-82/32 degrade every DB or authorization failure to null/empty via .catch(()=>null) rather than surfacing a raw error, matching opaque-upstream-errors' spirit for a public surface. Separately noted (not scored as a technique deviation): leaderboard/page.tsx:98-101 renders getDbMode()/dbModeLabel() ('Served live from Aurora DSQL') to every anonymous visitor of this crawlable public page — the SAME value api/health/route.ts:29-38 explicitly reasons 'describes deployment TOPOLOGY... shouldn't be handed to an anonymous caller' and gates behind CRON_SECRET. I did not mark this a deviation because it discloses only a coarse backend-family label (no hostname/credential/error-body), and the codebase treats it as a deliberate trust-building UI element (also on the landing page, IndexGallery.tsx) rather than an oversight — but it is a real inconsistency in how the project applies its own stated topology-disclosure rule, worth registry attention.

subjects.subject: rate-limiting
subjects.evidence: src/lib/rate-limit.ts:35 On the default self-hosted posture (no ASCENT_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS and no VERCEL witness), every anonymous caller of every per-IP door lands in one shared 'unknown' burst bucket with no spread layer, so ordinary traffic exhausts one caller's allowance together. Separately, every refusal does a fire-and-forget DB upsert, which puts a remote, per-request-billed write on the refusal hot path.

subjects.subject: cost-metering
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/credits.ts:434 When the debit's idempotency key already exists, consumeScanCredit returns a bare 'charged' (also at line 402) without checking whether that key's refund:<key> row exists. The store cannot tell an open attempt from a closed one, and there is no bounded attempt walk. Closed-key reuse is avoided only because callers mint keys per claim attempt or per UUID.

subjects.subject: untrusted-extension-host
subjects.evidence: src/lib/entitlement.ts:1 This context is a credit ledger, an owner-only grant route and a scan entitlement gate, so it has no extension install path, no isolation primitive and no foreign callbacks. A search of src/ for isolated-vm, quickjs, vm2, node:vm and extensionHost found no hits.

subjects.subject: cost-metering
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/usage.ts:169 The scan lane, the main spend class, is built only from persisted computed Scan rows. A scan whose provider calls failed or timed out and degraded to the `mock` engine (UNMETERED_PROVIDER) carries no tokens and is excluded, so failed-call spend in the scan lane leaves no row, which breaks 'failures are spend'.

subjects.subject: usage-analytics
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/kpi-metrics.ts:7 The Usage Metering context is billing metering (Scan rows and LLM-ledger calls aggregated per org and period for credits, showback and CSV reconciliation), not product-surface usage analytics; I searched the context's directories (src/app/usage, src/app/api/usage, src/lib/db, src/components/usage) for section_visited, sendBeacon, visibilitychange, NullSink and trackEvent and got zero hits, and a repo-wide search found no analytics vendor or emit door, consistent with this line, so the subject's precondition (an event vocabulary, session summaries and sinks measuring which surfaces users visit) does not hold here.

subjects.subject: measurement-honesty
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/usage.ts:544 A failed ledger read becomes an empty contribution, allowing the summary to publish partial usage without identifying the acquisition failure.

subjects.subject: data-retention
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/retention.ts:1005 The org receives scan counts only after the entire repo prune returns, so a later batch failure loses counts from earlier committed batches.

subjects.subject: settings
subjects.evidence: src/app/api/org/retention/route.ts:132 The retention change audit records the new policy without its prior values, preventing the trail from explaining or reverting the transition.

subjects.subject: feed
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/retention.ts:571 Control-observation retention protects one newest observation per entity through a fixed survivor predicate, whereas feed-retention requires the per-entity keep floor to be configurable.

subjects.subject: browser-credential-boundary
subjects.evidence: src/lib/db/client.ts reads DATABASE_URL/DSQL config via plain process.env, never NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed, and src/lib/db/index.ts:4 imports "server-only" so a client-component import of the DB barrel fails the build by design (comment cites ADR 2026-08-28-server-only-boundary); env.ts documents the NEXT_PUBLIC_ split explicitly. Prisma/DSQL is reached exclusively server-side — there is no browser-held credential or RLS-style policy engine fronting this store (unlike Supabase, which is deliberately regime-one for auth only, per supabase/client.ts:1-4 and .env.example:145).

subjects.subject: data-viz
subjects.evidence: src/components/ui/format.ts:32 The one shared delta classifier hardcodes the maturity-score noise band (SCORE_NOISE_BAND=2 points) and a rising-is-good polarity, with no way to pass either per metric. So callers showing other metrics work around it at the call site: CockpitDrivePanel colours deltaHex(debtDrop) but prints signedDelta(-debtDrop), DeliveryTrendPanelFoot passes a separate toneValue to get the colour right, and DeliveryActivityMomentum applies the 2-point score band to a percentage while drawing its own ▲/▼ arrow. That is exactly the per-call-site polarity and resolution fork that metric-identity warns about.
